questions.text:
Consider an Ethernet segment with a transmission speed of [latex]10^8[/latex] bits/sec and a
maximum segment length of 500 meters. If the speed of propagation of the signal
in the medium is [latex]2 \times 10^8[/latex] meters/sec, then the minimum frame size (in bits) required
for collision detection is _________
questions.solution:
For collision detection, transmission time must be at least the round-trip propagation time: [latex]\frac{L}{B}\ge2\frac{d}{v}[/latex]

[latex]T_p=\dfrac{500}{2\times10^8}=2.5\ \mu s[/latex]

[latex]L=2\times2.5\times10^{-6}\times10^8=500[/latex] bits

Answer: 500

questions.text:
Consider a TCP connection operating at a point of time with the congestion window
of size 12 MSS (Maximum Segment Size), when a timeout occurs due to packet
loss. Assuming that all the segments transmitted in the next two RTTs (Round Trip
Time) are acknowledged correctly, the congestion window size (in MSS) during the
third RTT will be _________
questions.solution:
On timeout: [latex]ssthresh=12/2=6[/latex] MSS and cwnd resets to 1 MSS, then slow start (doubling each RTT):

- RTT 1: cwnd = 1
- RTT 2: cwnd = 2
- RTT 3: cwnd = 4 (still below ssthresh = 6)

Answer: 4

questions.text: Which  one  of  the  following  CIDR  prefixes  exactly  represents  the  range  of IP addresses 10.12.2.0 to 10.12.3.255?
questions.solution:
10.12.2.0 to 10.12.3.255 has [latex]2\times256=512=2^9[/latex] addresses, so host bits = 9 and prefix = [latex]32-9=23[/latex].

Third octet: 2 = 00000010, 3 = 00000011 [latex]\text{---}[/latex] the first 23 bits are the same, so the block is aligned.

(/24 covers only 10.12.2.x; /22 covers 10.12.0.0-10.12.3.255.)

Answer: 10.12.2.0/23

questions.text: Which of the following fields of an IP header is/are always modified by any router before it forwards the IP packet?
questions.solution:
Every router decrements the TTL. Since a header field changed, the header checksum must be recomputed too.

Source IP and protocol are not changed by an ordinary router (source IP changes only with NAT, which is not "any router").

Answer: TTL, Header Checksum

questions.text: Which of the following statements about IPv4 fragmentation is/are TRUE?
questions.solution:
Recall the IPv4 fragmentation rules:
- In IPv4, any router whose outgoing link MTU is smaller than the datagram can fragment it (not only the source).
- Fragments may take different routes, so reassembly is done only at the destination.

Answer: Options 2 and 3

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: The fragmentation of an IP datagram is performed only at the source of the datagram
The fragmentation of an IP datagram is performed at any IP router which finds that the size of the datagram to be transmitted exceeds the MTU
The reassembly of fragments is performed only at the destination of the datagram
The reassembly of fragments is performed at all intermediate routers along the path from the source to the destination
